{{short description|Swiss mathematician and teacher}}
'''David Rytz von Brugg''' (1 April 1801, in [[:de:Bucheggberg|Bucheggberg]] – 25 March 1868, in [[Aarau]]) was a  Swiss [[mathematician]] and [[teacher]].<ref>Ostermann and Wanner mention in ''„Geometry by Its History“'' (S. 69) his  firstname as ''„Daniel“''.</ref>

== Life ==
Rytz von Brugg was son of a  [[priest]] and studied [[mathematics]] at [[Göttingen]] and [[Leipzig]]. He had teaching positions at various cities, one of them 1835 until 1862 at Aarau, where he was ''„Professor der Mathematik an der Gewerbeschule zu Aarau“''.<ref name="AO-GW">Alexander Ostermann, Gerhard Wanner: ''Geometry by Its History.'' 2012, S. 69</ref>

== Merits ==
Rytz von Brugg is famous for a geometrical method which is known as [[Rytz's construction|Rytz’s axis construction]]. This classical procedure retrieves the semi-axes of an [[Ellipse]] from any pair of [[conjugate diameters]]. This method is known since 1845, when it was published within a paper by Leopold Moosbrugger.<ref name="SG-HJI-KHS">Siegfried Gottwald, Hans-Joachim Ilgauds, Karl-Heinz Schlote (Hrsg.): ''Lexikon bedeutender Mathematiker.'' 1990, S. 407</ref><ref>Emil Müller und Erwin Kruppa ''Lehrbuch der darstellenden Geometrie.'' 1961, S. 98 .</ref>
